liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Black Peter** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls Black Peter among the finest ever played, edging only the 12/13/80 version; Reviewer calls the Black Peter on this audience recording scary good [5][14]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Described as very hot [7]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Guitar break outro is outstanding; from 'Run and see' onward it is one of the better, longer versions [16]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Called epic by this reviewer [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **Nobody's Fault But Mine**: back after 136 archived shows (1171 days) [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-10-12.sbd.goodbear.3919.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 23 songs; 151 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Goodbear transfer judged weak, though the master is good; reviewer says their own old reel sounds better; Taping equipment problems apparently affected The Promised Land and the encore [1][15]
- **gd77-10-12.sbd.cotsman.19291.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 154 min; rated 4.17/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Audience recording used to fill gaps in the soundboard is described as very poor; Soundboard tape is spotty and drops into a rough, beaten audience source, especially toward the end [5][7]
- **gd1977-10-12.121618.set2.aud.miller.flac1644**: audience recording; 12 songs; 98 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [3]
- **gd1977-10-12.121616.set2.aud.miller.flac1648**: audience recording; 12 songs; 98 min [4]

## Around the show

- Manor Downs was a small racetrack outside Austin, built hoping betting would arrive in Texas, which came only in the 90s [8]
- A high school rodeo with teenage bronc riders ran at the same time as the concert [8]
- Attendee recalls it was cold on arrival and freezing by showtime; fans warmed themselves around fires in oil drums [9]
- Venue is out in the country beyond Austin, in the boonies [9]
- Reviewer grew up about 10 miles from Manor Downs; a hippie uncle attended this show [11]
- Reviewer says the band kept a cold crowd warm in many different ways [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-10-12.sbd.goodbear.3919.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Teddy Goodbear; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Goodbear encoded and posted this as SHN files to the binaries newsgroups [1]
- **gd77-10-12.sbd.cotsman.19291.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Soundboard source goes through a cassette-based chain to CD, EAC and SHN, patched with audience source via J. Cotsman; S. Milewski supplied the audience patches [2]
- **gd1977-10-12.121618.set2.aud.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Unknown Mics -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [3]
- **gd1977-10-12.121616.set2.aud.miller.flac1648**: taped by Jonathan Rozes; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Unknown Mics -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat (48k) [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by SF Rock Posters & Collectibles: [AUCTION - Grateful Dead - Michael Priest - Manor Downs Texas - 1977 Poster - Excellent](https://rockposters.com/products/auction-grateful-dead-manor-downs-texas-michael-priest-1977-poster-excellent?variant=47812629725463) [18]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [current-page:url:arg:3 | Grateful Dead](https://www.dead.net/tags/manor-downs) [19]
- Poster by SF Rock Posters & Collectibles: [AUCTION - Grateful Dead - Michael Priest - Manor Downs Texas - 1977 Poster - Excellent](https://rockposters.com/products/auction-grateful-dead-manor-downs-texas-michael-priest-1977-poster-excellent?variant=47812629725463) [20]
